title: Mayasaba Tauri request and response payload type definitions
rule: Every type name referenced by payloads.json request_fields must resolve here. Types are declared as operations gain declared request fields, not speculatively: an operation that does not declare request_fields has no payload type yet, and inventing one would be a declaration nothing consumes. A type is also declared for an operation that is implemented end to end, because that is when the shape exists on the wire and can be checked against the declaration instead of asserted (DEC-056).

DeliveryCounts.title: How many of a project's messages are unfinished, by state
DeliveryCounts.description: Terminal and successful states are deliberately absent: this is a health view, and a count of everything would answer a different question. dead_lettered is counted from the dead_letters table, which is the durable dead-letter record.

OpenGap.title: A position missing between two observed positions in one message stream
OpenGap.description: Derived from messages and never stored, because the positions are already durable there and a second record of the same fact is a second fact that can disagree. expected is the absent position; found is the observed position that revealed it, which is always present because the walk stops at the stream's highest position. code is the registry key SEQUENCE_GAP, carried in the value so the wire needs no second lookup (DEC-055).

ProjectBriefDraft.title: The user's stated project intent, submitted at project creation

body.description: Non-empty project intent. pattern \S rejects whitespace-only input, which is the structural half of the rule; whether the text constitutes meaningful intent is a domain judgement owned by the intake router, not a schema concern.

source.description: How the intent was captured. Defaults to INITIAL_INTAKE_COMPOSER.

ProjectPathDraft.title: A task-scoped path allowed within the project's authorized workspace

path.description: Workspace-relative or absolute path inside the authorized workspace. Workspace/task-path scope is authoritative; a path outside the authorized scope is refused by policy, not by this schema.

purpose.description: Why the path is in scope.

ProjectView.title: The authoritative project projection the Control Room displays
ProjectView.description: A projection of stored state, never UI-side draft state, and one shape rather than one per operation: create_project and list_projects return the same projection, because a created project and a listed project that differed in shape would be two descriptions of one thing. There is no name field on the request side; the display name here is derived by the owning service from the validated canonical workspace folder leaf (DEC-050). Every field is required and always present: a nullable field is sent as null rather than omitted, so a caller can tell "no brief" from "this build does not send briefs".

project_id.description: Generated independently of the path; never derived from it (DEC-050).

name.description: Display name derived from the canonical workspace folder leaf.

local_path.description: The canonicalized workspace root that was persisted, not the spelling the caller sent.

current_epoch.description: The project's current epoch. It is the project's epoch, not the epoch at creation, so a listed project reports the epoch it is in now.

brief_id.description: ProjectBrief version 1. The project cannot exist without it, so null here means the stored row is inconsistent.

RecoveryIssue.title: One finding from the startup recovery scan

kind.description: A machine-readable finding kind, so the Control Room does not classify findings by reading their prose.

CommandError.title: The payload of a rejected invocation, for every operation
CommandError.description: Every command and query returns either its declared response payload or this shape, which is why it is declared once rather than per operation: it is not operation-specific. code is the canonical key of an entry in schemas/error-v1/registry.json, which is where the category, retryability, severity and meaning of each code live - the enum is deliberately not repeated here, because a second copy of the code vocabulary would be a competing source of truth (DEC-021). A caller branches on code, never on message.

code.description: A registered code from schemas/error-v1/registry.json. The gate fails if the implementation produces a code the registry does not declare (DEC-055).

message.description: Human-readable detail. Never parsed: the code carries the meaning.

create_projectRequest.title: Create a project from its local workspace, atomically
create_projectRequest.description: There is deliberately no name field. The human-readable project display name is derived by ProjectService from the validated canonical workspace folder name, so the caller cannot supply identity metadata that disagrees with the filesystem (DEC-050). project_id is generated independently and is never derived from a path.

local_path.description: Candidate local workspace folder. Mayasaba is local-only; a non-local or remote path is refused by policy (DEC-004). Validated and canonicalized by the service, which also derives the display name from it.

initial_brief.description: Persisted as ProjectBrief version 1 in the same transaction as the project row, the initial epoch and the PROJECT_CREATED event.

project_paths.description: Optional additional in-scope paths. Defaults to the workspace root only.

create_projectResponse.title: The authoritative state that exists after project creation committed
create_projectResponse.description: The projection declared once as ProjectView, so a created project and a listed project cannot drift apart in shape. This name is kept as an alias rather than deleted, because payloads.json declares it as the operation's response type and a declared identifier is not removed to save a level of indirection.

list_projectsResponse.title: Every persisted project, newest first
list_projectsResponse.description: An array of the same projection create_project returns. It is a distinct declared type rather than a second name for ProjectView because the two responses genuinely differ: one is a project and the other is a list of them.

get_recovery_statusResponse.title: The startup recovery scan result
get_recovery_statusResponse.description: Recovery reports and never repairs, so this is a report rather than a repair outcome. clean is true only when the scan found nothing; integrity_ok reports whether SQLite's own integrity check passed, which is a different question from whether the stored rows agree with each other, and the two are separate fields so neither can be inferred from the other. An empty issues list with clean false is not a state this scan produces.

clean.description: True when the scan found no inconsistencies in stored state.

integrity_ok.description: Whether SQLite's integrity check passed. False means the durable file itself is suspect.

get_communication_healthRequest.title: Read one project's durable communication health
get_communication_healthRequest.description: Read-only. Names the project whose communication state is reported.

get_communication_healthResponse.title: One project's durable communication health
get_communication_healthResponse.description: Every value is read or derived from the durable record. backlog and enqueue_limit are global rather than per-project, because the capacity bound the bus enforces is global (DEC-068); counts and open_gaps are scoped to the requested project. open_gaps is derived from messages and never stored, so it cannot disagree with the record it describes. transport_status is not_connected because no agent transport exists until M3, and reporting anything else would imply something was contacted (DEC-073).

backlog.description: Outstanding dispatch work across all projects.

enqueue_limit.description: The bound backlog is measured against, read from the bus's own dispatch policy rather than copied.

get_event_cursorRequest.title: Read a consumer's durable position in one project's event stream
get_event_cursorRequest.description: Read-only. Identifies one consumer of one project.

get_event_cursorResponse.title: A consumer's durable event position
get_event_cursorResponse.description: The canonical cursor shape (schemas/ui-events-v1/cursor.schema.json) rather than a second definition of it; that schema sets additionalProperties false, so these six fields are the whole wire shape. last_sequence is 0 when no cursor row exists, which is what the absence of a row truthfully implies - the canonical schema has no field in which to distinguish an absent row from a row at zero, and the error registry has no NOT_FOUND code, so that limitation is recorded rather than papered over. next_sequence, gap_detected and resync_from are reported empty because event_cursors stores only last_sequence and no contract defines how they would be derived; inventing a derivation would put a number on the wire that nothing durable supports.

get_council_roundRequest.title: Read one council round together with its decision-quality records
get_council_roundRequest.description: The existing query, extended rather than duplicated: DEC-052 requires outcome data to be observable read-only, and a second query would have been a second read surface for one concept. The response carries the controller-computed records (mode selection, round roles, claim grades, budget state) and the append-only outcome records. All of it is informational: no field here may influence routing, thresholds, mode selection or authority.

include_outcomes.description: Include the decision-outcome records for decisions taken from this round. Suppressing them is a presentation choice, never a state change, because the record is append-only.

get_council_roundResponse.title: A council round with its controller-computed quality records
get_council_roundResponse.description: Every quality record here is computed or assigned by the controller and persisted by CouncilService. None of it is agent-supplied, and none of it grants authority.

mode_selection.description: The ModeSelection record for this decision point. Null when the decision point is non-material and no record was required. A SOLO decision point has a record and no round, so it is reported rather than omitted.

assigned_reason.description: Why this agent holds this role, including LINEAGE_UNAVOIDABLE when the skeptic could not be drawn from a different lineage group than the leading proposal's author.

budget.description: Derived from council_budget_ledger. Wall-clock excludes paused intervals and records them separately; a token figure whose adapter reported nothing is UNAVAILABLE rather than estimated, and tokens_used is then null.

outcomes.description: Append-only, derived only from controller facts: a validation result, the reopen_decision command, or decision supersession. HELD carries a validation evidence reference.

offline_agent_ids.description: Participants currently paused as offline or dropped. A paused interval is excluded from the wall-clock budget and recorded; silence is never agreement.

validate_workspaceRequest.title: Validate a candidate workspace folder without persisting anything
validate_workspaceRequest.description: Read-only. Rust validates and canonicalizes the candidate and returns a check result; nothing is created and nothing is written, so a path that does not exist can never come back AUTHORIZED. This runs before a project exists and feeds create_project, which re-validates the same path rather than trusting this answer.

path.description: The candidate folder the user selected or typed. A UNC or other network path is refused as not-local (DEC-004).

validate_workspaceResponse.title: The authoritative outcome of validating a workspace candidate
validate_workspaceResponse.description: AUTHORIZED means the folder exists, is local, is a directory and could be canonicalized; it does not authorize every operation inside it, because task-scoped paths, policy and leases remain narrower (DEC-048). On INVALID, code carries the machine-readable WorkspaceRejection and the path fields are null. Field names are snake_case, and they are the names that actually cross the Tauri boundary: the Rust struct serializes with #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")] and the command takes its arguments with #[tauri::command(rename_all = "snake_case")], so the contract, the wire and the frontend all spell a field the same way and nothing renames it in transit (DEC-054).

canonical_path.description: Absolute, normalized path; null on INVALID. This is the spelling create_project persists.

requested_path.description: The path exactly as the caller supplied it, before normalization.

derived_project_name.description: The display name derived from the canonical folder leaf (DEC-050); null on INVALID.

code.description: A machine-readable rejection code (WORKSPACE_*); null on AUTHORIZED.

message.description: A human-readable rejection message; null on AUTHORIZED.

error.title: What every operation returns instead of its response payload when it is rejected
error.description: Declared once rather than per operation, because a rejection is not operation-specific. See CommandError for why code is not enumerated here.
